story.title: Muscat Stock Exchange Leads GCC Markets for a Second Year as Asyad Shipping Draws Strong Investor Demand

detail.extracted_title: Muscat Stock Exchange Leads GCC Markets for a Second Year as Asyad Shipping Draws Strong Investor Demand
detail.article_html:
A 303 percent surge in nine-month trading value to OMR 9.757 billion, rising banking earnings, and three-times oversubscribed retail demand for Asyad Shipping highlight growing depth in Oman's capital market.

With less than two months remaining in 2026, the Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) is on course to record the strongest annual performance among Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) financial markets for the second consecutive year. Following a 28 percent gain in 2025 that brought the benchmark index to 5,867 points, the MSX index has climbed an additional 23 percent since the start of 2026, closing Thursday's trading session at 7,276.41 points. Over the same period in 2026, other GCC equity benchmarks recorded declines ranging between 3.9 percent and 12.2 percent.

Market data from the first nine months of 2026 shows a broad expansion in liquidity and institutional participation. Total trading value surged by 303 percent to reach OMR 9.757 billion, compared with OMR 2.421 billion during the same nine-month period in 2025. Total traded volume rose 153 percent to 33.43 billion shares, up from 13.2 billion shares a year earlier. Average daily trading value across 2026 has reached OMR 52 million—rising from OMR 41 million in September to OMR 61 million in October as monthly trading value climbed 41 percent to OMR 1.2 billion—lifting total market capitalization to OMR 38.7 billion.

Credit Upgrades, Emerging Market Watchlist, and Liquidity Reforms

Analysts point to a series of fiscal and regulatory milestones behind the sustained rally. Standard & Poor's recently affirmed Oman's investment-grade credit rating, while both the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank raised their projections for Omani economic growth in 2026. International index provider FTSE Russell also placed the Muscat Stock Exchange on its official watchlist for a potential upgrade from Frontier Market to Emerging Market status, drawing heightened attention from regional and foreign institutional funds.

Domestic capital market reforms have reinforced that momentum. The issuance of Oman's new Securities Law and the announcement of the Oman Financial Centre have modernized regulatory oversight, while the market-making and liquidity-enhancement initiatives led by the Tanmia Liquidity Fund—launched in 2024 by Oman National Investments Development Company (Tanmia) in partnership with regional investment bank SICO—have deepened order books across listed equities.

"Strong corporate earnings, fiscal discipline, and structural liquidity initiatives have positioned the Muscat Stock Exchange at the forefront of GCC financial markets for two consecutive years, lifting total market capitalization to OMR 38.7 billion."

— Amal Rajab, Financial Market Analysis in Oman Daily

Banking Sector Growth and the Asyad Shipping Offering

Corporate earnings across listed Omani firms have supported the rise in share valuations. Following a 12 percent increase in total net profits across listed companies during the first half of 2026, six of the seven banks listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange posted higher nine-month earnings. Combined net profits for the seven banks rose 8.2 percent year-on-year to reach OMR 455 million during the first nine months of 2026.

Investor appetite was equally evident this week as the Financial Services Authority (FSA) approved the share allocation results for the secondary public offering of Asyad Shipping Company. The offering placed 335,312,913 existing shares—representing 6.44 percent of the company's issued share capital—at an offer price of 195 baisas per share.

Retail participation exceeded initial projections: 11,205 individual applications subscribed for 194,293,900 shares valued at OMR 37.887 million, representing roughly three times the initial retail allocation. In response to this demand, the retail tranche was expanded by 15 percent from 65.11 million shares to 74.88 million shares. Under the FSA-approved allocation policy designed to protect small savers, retail applicants in the small-investor tier received a guaranteed minimum of 4,000 shares plus 19.4 percent of their remaining requested shares, while large individual investors received 30.8 percent of their subscribed shares alongside 260.44 million shares allocated to local and regional institutional investors.

Sources

  • Oman Daily
detail.instagram_caption:
The Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) is on track to record the strongest annual performance among all GCC equity markets for the second consecutive year. After surging 28 percent in 2025, the MSX benchmark index has climbed another 23 percent since the start of 2026 to reach 7,276.41 points, while total trading value in the first nine months of 2026 jumped 303 percent year-on-year to OMR 9.757 billion across 33.43 billion traded shares.

Backed by Standard & Poor's investment-grade rating affirmation, FTSE Russell's watchlist inclusion for Emerging Market status, the new Securities Law, the Tanmia Liquidity Fund, and an 8.2 percent rise in nine-month net profits across Oman's seven listed banks to OMR 455 million, total market capitalization has reached OMR 38.7 billion.

That confidence was reflected this week as the Financial Services Authority approved allocations for Asyad Shipping Company's secondary offering of 335.31 million shares at 195 baisas per share. Retail investors submitted 11,205 applications worth OMR 37.887 million—roughly three times the initial retail tranche—prompting a 15 percent increase in the individual investor allocation to broaden public ownership.
